angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 544,524 km at 28.28 pc = 0.26 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 35.3581 +/- 0.0159 mas (same row, RUWE 0.89): 28.28 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.7827 +/- 0.0329 solar radii from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 207897 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract): 544,524 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.8208 +/- 0.0226 solar masses from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 207897 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5106 +/- 67 K from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 207897 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 207897 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-207897.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.565, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 207897 (pscomppars): spectral type K0 V, from Heidari et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...658A.176H/abstract)

luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 207897 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.42136, from MacDougall et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 207897 (pscomppars): age 4.7 Gyr, from MacDougall et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)
